how: Calls recruit helpers to start a she slime and recover it after destruction.
A difficult Dragonlord attempt prompts an explicit judgment that many people must coordinate.
A brief promise to watch directly answers the request for someone to keep an eye on the slime.
The watching request receives an explicit commitment, without establishing a general preference between acceptance and refusal.
The call for help making a she slime receives replies committing pixels and reporting contributions.
Members propose several figures and additions rather than one settled collective design.
A member begins a she slime and another commits pixels to that project.
Beginning a she slime and calling for helpers occur within the same utterance.
Participants report hours of work paying off and claim a made picture while thanking helpers.
Members locate work with coordinates and supply or request reference pictures and templates.
Separate locating the work from specifying its pixels because coordinate-only recruitment can still leave helpers requesting a template.
The record shows a template requested after coordinates but does not establish its provision or adoption as a settled design.
Participants contest bot-driven movement, automated overwriting, and an alleged protection shutdown.
Constant attack and a running repair script are explicitly connected while additional human help remains welcome.
Machine assistance requires agreement over its task and sequence plus continued operator support, since automated work can overwrite repairs or cease during attack.
Personal responsibility for agreements and bot operation does not establish formal organizational decisions or test the cross-room prevalence claim.
Members watch while awake, ask for defenders, and repair damaged pixels.
A participant reports building effort paying off and immediately requests ongoing watching against damage.
An accused damaging placer explains an accidental repair attempt and receives an apology, requiring attribution correction within the local account.

statement: Giving up when others undo repairs
how: A participant withdraws because others repeatedly reverse corrective pixels, adding an exit mechanism that does not require a judgment of insufficient hands.
Moving the slime requires permission, agreement from neighbors, and completing a related portal project.
A reported takeover is held off while participants discuss the slime with neighboring groups.
Participants report carrying a proposal into another group's discussion and returning with a conditional Discord response.
Negotiators must reconcile conflicting permission reports across venues before treating relocation as approved.
Implementing a relocation agreement requires following the agreed sequence rather than treating permission alone as completion.
Disputed permission and bot implementation do not establish a dispute over a representative's right to bind every placer.
The negotiation cannot establish an ensuing representation dispute when the recorded objections concern permission and execution.
A compromise relocates the slime with an explicit warning that overwriting will occur during the move.
Allow negotiated relocation during defense, conditional on neighboring permission and portal completion, without requiring a completed loss or manpower-driven retreat.
Difficulty defending and a negotiated move are visible, but the concepts do not establish too few hands as the cause of that move.
Outside participants offer help and defenders from another group are recruited and later credited.
A plea that an erasure cannot be stopped alone receives an explicit report that outside defenders are helping.
Negotiating the move produces a conditional offer to help with the neighboring portal before moving the slime.
A participant explicitly reports an existing alliance while requesting further help preserving the slime.
An already existing alliance is reported during defense, leaving its formation and the reason for joining unobserved.
Host approval rules govern the slime's claimed location even while some placers allegedly ignore its approved status.
A visitor apologizes for apparent aggression while seeking agreement, and defenders appeal to damaging placers to stop.
An apology accompanies seeking agreement rather than demonstrating restraint caused by an already settled border.
Game lore gives defense and gratitude recognizable language about experience, escaping monsters, and human or slime helpers.
Game lore accompanies defending the picture but does not name a prior rival in a call to attack.
The reported takeover and neighboring discussions do not establish an inherited quarrel.
Public building and defense calls do not establish any moderator boundary around canvas talk.
Calls alone cannot establish either a canvas flood or a resulting host response.
Game jokes during defense do not establish host-sub April Fools framing.
Members thank contributors, claim labor, and value shared work even after a project is destroyed.
Recognition includes celebrating news that the picture appeared in an outside fandom venue, without demonstrating help from that venue.
The maker explicitly credits the people who built and protected the picture for its outcome.
Participants report destruction and mourn the lost slime.
End notices and final-canvas reports distinguish the surviving Liquid Metal Slime from another destroyed project.
Track separate works through different fates so one project's loss does not turn another project's survival into a contradictory community account.
End reporting and credit share one turn while loss reports arise separately, leaving celebration as a cause of later preservation unestablished.
Survival and thanks do not establish a decision to carry the effort into later canvases, emblems, or enduring ties.
A final-canvas report does not establish a subsequent continuation decision.
Fate reports and a post-close apology about an accidental pixel do not establish cleanup of a retained canvas or correction of a public historical account.
Receiving an invasion and asking damaging users to stop do not establish an outgoing attack organized by the room.
Recruitment is visible but its conversion into an outgoing attack is unobserved.
An apology following an explanation of accidental repair cannot test restraint caused by the room's attack call.
A permission request amid defense does not establish negotiation caused by an outgoing attack.
Retrospective complaints recount a takeover and automated overwriting, carrying the contested encounter into talk after the close.
Retrospective grievance after defending against encroachment does not establish contention caused by the room's outgoing attack.
